messages.subject: Linear predictors
parts:
Dear All,
 
I am trying to implement a specific model integrating fixed effects, random effects and a spline function based on B-spline basies. For estimating the coefficients associated to B-splines I am using a linear predictor.
 
The model looks as follows:
 
\eta_{ij} = mu + v_i+u_j + \sum_{k =1}^{K} \beta_k B^d_k(x_{ij})  (1)
 
with u_j a "simple" random effect, and v_i a fixed effect.( Here it is a simplified version of the right model, but it just to point out my problem. )
 
If I have just this model:
 
\eta_{ij} = mu +\sum_{k =1}^{K} \beta_k B^d_k(x_{ij}) (2)
 
I am using the following INLA argument "control.predictor = list(A= cBind(rep(1, nrow(B)), B),compute=TRUE, link=1) where B is a matrix containing the values of the B-splines at each point.  But when I am coming back to the model (1) I don't know how I can integrate u_j and v_i without linear predictor ? It seems that it will be something like the argument "effects" in the function "inla.stack"...
 
Thanks for your help,
Regards,
Marie.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear predictors
parts:
Yes, inla.stack might help. I'm not sure what you mean by "integrate ... without linear predictor", but the model could be setup like this:

stack=inla.stack(data=list(y=y),
  A=list(cBind(1, B), Diagonal(length(uidx)), Diagonal(length(vidx))),
  effects=list(list(mu=1, beta=1:ncol(B)), list(u=uidx), list(v=vidx))

# extract info to be used in the inla() call:
data=inla.stack.data(stack)
A=inla.stack.A(stack)

formula = y ~ -1 + mu + f(u, model="iid") + f(v, model="iid") + f(beta, model=?, ?)
(With whatever model you use for beta)

Note that mu and beta are confounded unless you've modified the Bspline basis to be orthogonal to a constant. But that's a general modelling issue, not specific to inla, so the solution to that problem depends on what model you really want.

Finn
